newsitem.title: UK: Couple guilty of Bank of England cheque theft.
newsitem.headline: Couple guilty of Bank of England cheque theft.

text.p: A British couple who came very close to cashing a cheque for 9.7 million pounds ($15.7 million) stolen from the Bank of England were convicted of fraud on Wednesday.

Business consultant Peter Garnett and his accountant wife Linda thought they had got away with their audacious plan. But they were found out at the last minute after their commercial bank became suspicious about their finances and lavish lifestyle.
London's Guildhall crown court was told the cheque was believed to be the only one stolen from Britain's central bank since it was founded in the 17th century.

The Garnetts showed no emotion as the jury unanimously convicted them of conspiring to defraud between January and December 1994. They could each be given prison terms of up to 10 years in jail when they are sentenced on November 23.
Linda Garnett, 52, will also face sentence on 15 counts of theft she admitted which involved syphoning more than 73,000 pounds from the veterinary practice where she worked.
This helped finance a lifestyle involving driving a Rolls-Royce, a Jaguar and a Mercedes-Benz, owning four houses and apartments and expensive holidays overseas.

The week-long trial heard that the first anybody knew a cheque had been stolen from the Bank of England was when Garnett, 54, tried to pay it into his wife's Midland Bank business account in Grantham, a town in central England.

The cheque had been stolen from a chequebook kept at the Bank of England to purchase certificates of deposit. It bore two expertly forged signatures of bank officials. Despite extensive inquiries, the thief was never discovered.

The Garnetts would probably have got away with their plan but for a "marker" which Midland staff had placed on their account. It had been put there as a reminder to be on the lookout for possible suspicious transactions.
Inquiries were made with the Bank of England and it was quickly discovered the cheque had been stolen.
Police were waiting for Garnett when he returned to the Grantham branch to withdraw 50,000 pounds three days after he had paid in the 9.7 million. ($1=.6165 Pound)
